content: At least eight people were killed and 26 others injured when a passenger bus plunged nearly 100 metres into a gorge in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand early on Tuesday, officials said. The bus broke through a roadside railing near Gular Bazaar in Tehri Garhwal district and fell into a stream below a bridge on the Rishikesh-Badrinath National Highway, one of the main pilgrimage routes into the Himalayan foothills. The accident happened at around 4.30 a.m. local time, when the bus was travelling from Haridwar towards Chamoli with an estimated 30 to 35 passengers on board, according to [The Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/uttarakhand/6-killed-20-injured-as-bus-falls-into-ravine-in-uttarakhands-tehri-garhwal/). Seven passengers died at the scene, and one more succumbed to injuries after being taken to hospital, Tehri Garhwal police said. The figures were revised during the morning as rescue teams reached the wreckage: early reports put the death toll at six, before officials confirmed eight dead and 26 injured. Teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), stationed at Byasi and Dhalwala, reached the site quickly and carried the injured up from the gorge on stretchers across difficult terrain before transferring them to ambulances. The SDRF said 26 injured passengers were brought out of the ravine, and the search operation at the site was subsequently concluded. Of the injured, 17 were taken to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in Rishikesh and nine to the Government Hospital in Rishikesh, according to officials quoted by The Tribune. AIIMS said 22 patients had been received by the hospital, including two who were declared dead on arrival, and that six patients were assessed as being in critical condition in the initial examination. District Magistrate Nitika Khandelwal said the administration had received information about the accident on Tuesday morning and immediately dispatched SDRF and district administration teams to carry out the rescue. The bus, operated by Vishwanath Seva, had departed Haridwar at around 3.30 a.m., according to local reports, meaning it had been on the road for about an hour when it lost control near Gular Bridge. What caused the crash has not been officially established. A survivor, however, has alleged that speed played a part. Pankaj, an injured passenger, told the news agency ANI that the driver was driving at high speed and that passengers had asked him two or three times to slow down before the vehicle went out of control, according to [The Statesman](https://www.thestatesman.com/india/uttarakhand-bus-accident-8-dead-26-injured-in-tehri-gorge-1503663395.html). Officials have not confirmed that account, and the cause of the accident remains under investigation. The allegation, if borne out, would point to a familiar pattern on Uttarakhand's mountain roads, where buses on narrow, winding highways above deep valleys have repeatedly gone off the road with heavy loss of life. The Rishikesh-Badrinath highway carries a constant flow of pilgrims and tourists heading for the Char Dham shrines, and early-morning departures are common as operators try to cover long distances before dark. The crash was not the only fatal accident in the state on Tuesday morning. In a separate incident in Rudraprayag district, four people were killed and six injured when a Bolero vehicle returning from a wedding ceremony plunged into a gorge on the Kandara motor road in the Kyunja Valley of Agastyamuni block, officials said. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed grief over the loss of lives in the multiple road accidents in the state, including the one near Gular in Tehri Garhwal, and district officials, including the Tehri district magistrate and the superintendent of police, visited AIIMS Rishikesh to check on the condition of the injured. The twin accidents on the same morning underline the risks of travel on the state's hill roads, where a single loss of control can turn into a fall of a hundred metres. For the families of the eight people who died near Gular, and for the 26 injured now in hospital in Rishikesh, the wait is for the names of the victims and for an official answer to the question the survivor has already raised: whether the bus was travelling too fast for a dark, narrow mountain road at half past four in the morning. The morning's events in India came on a day when the world's attention was also turning to Asia for diplomacy, with Quad leaders meeting in Manila and a landmark [trilateral summit between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia due to open in Shenzhen on November 19](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/xi-trump-putin-summit-shenzhen-november-19). Closer to the region, a powerful [magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck off Indonesia's Tual earlier on Tuesday](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/indonesia-earthquake-tual-magnitude-6-6-november-2026), shaking island communities and sending tremors as far as Darwin in northern Australia, though no casualties were reported there.
summary: Eight people were killed and 26 injured when a passenger bus plunged nearly 100 metres into a gorge near Gular Bazaar in Uttarakhand's Tehri Garhwal district early on Tuesday; a survivor alleges passengers repeatedly asked the driver to slow down, though officials have not established the cause.
title: Eight killed, 26 injured as bus plunges 100 metres into gorge in India's Uttarakhand
